question: Why is herd immunity super important for young babies and people with weak immune systems?

options.A: They produce antibodies much faster than healthy adults
options.B: They live in environments with zero exposure to pathogens
options.C: They cannot safely receive certain vaccines themselves
options.D: They require higher doses of medication to build immunity

explanation: Spot on! When most people around them are vaccinated, it builds a protective shield for those who can't take the shots yet.

question: What is the main job of Type I taste cells?

options.A: To serve as basal stem cells for cellular regeneration
options.B: To house G-protein coupled receptors for bitter compounds
options.C: To form direct chemical synapses detecting sour tastants
options.D: To act as supporting cells and clear neurotransmitters

explanation: Type I cells act like supportive helpers (similar to glial cells in the nervous system) by taking care of neighboring taste cells and clearing out extra chemicals.

question: What is a nurse assessing when checking a patient's neurological status during an exam?

options.A: The presence of bowel sounds in four quadrants
options.B: Orientation, reflexes, and overall mental function
options.C: The strength and rhythm of the apical pulse
options.D: The rate of air exchange in the lower lung lobes

explanation: Neurological checks look at brain function, nerve responses, and sensory processing to ensure the nervous system is working properly. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h6)

question: On a CT scan, how does dense bone usually appear?

options.A: Pitch black
options.B: Bright white
options.C: Bright green
options.D: Transparent

explanation: Bone absorbs a lot of radiation, so it shows up as a bright white color on the image. You've got this!

question: What is the main job of a mechanical ventilator in the hospital ward?

options.A: To support or replace spontaneous breathing
options.B: To permanently eliminate the need for oxygen therapy
options.C: To cure underlying pulmonary infections
options.D: To lower systemic blood pressure safely

explanation: Think of the ventilator as an extra pair of lungs for patients who are too tired or sick to breathe well on their own. It takes over or helps out until they recover!

question: A woman in labor in a remote village has a uterine rupture, but the family cannot find a vehicle to take her to the hospital. Which delay does this represent?

options.A: Delay in diagnosing the initial pregnancy
options.B: Delay in receiving adequate treatment at the hospital
options.C: Delay in deciding to seek care
options.D: Delay in reaching a medical facility

explanation: You nailed it. Distance, bad roads, and transport troubles fall squarely under the second delay—getting from home to a health facility.

question: What does the term asepsis mean?

options.A: The presence of helpful bacteria on the skin
options.B: The absence of disease-producing microorganisms
options.C: The complete destruction of all body cells
options.D: The growth of pathogens in a wound

explanation: Asepsis literally translates to a- (without) sepsis (poison or infection), meaning the absence of harmful germs. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h1)

question: In global polio campaigns, what does the abbreviation 'AFP' stand for?

options.A: Asymmetrical Facial Palsy
options.B: Active Fever Protocol
options.C: Advanced Functional Pathology
options.D: Acute Flaccid Paralysis

question: When a community health nurse speaks up for marginalized villagers who lack clean water, what nursing role is being demonstrated?

options.A: Pharmacologist
options.B: Surgeon
options.C: Advocate
options.D: Administrator

explanation: Advocacy involves speaking up, defending, and fighting for the rights and health needs of vulnerable or voiceless populations. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h8)

question: What makes writing patient notes (charting) tricky for flight nurses during a journey?

options.A: A complete lack of paper and pens in the cabin
options.B: Constant aircraft motion and turbulence
options.C: Patients refusing to share their medical history
options.D: Strict laws forbidding written notes in aircraft

explanation: Right on! Trying to write neat, legible notes while the aircraft is shaking and bumping from turbulence is definitely a challenge.

question: Why is executive leadership commitment critical months after a project has started?

options.A: It allows directors to change the hospital rules every single week
options.B: It guarantees that the hospital will receive international financial grants
options.C: It stops nurses from taking their mandatory annual leave days
options.D: It shows staff that leadership cares about the change beyond the initial launch

question: How should chronic pain medication be scheduled for a palliative care patient?

options.A: Only when the patient cries out in pain
options.B: Around the clock to maintain steady relief
options.C: Only when vital signs begin to spike
options.D: Strictly once every 24 hours in the morning

explanation: Giving pain meds around the clock prevents pain from spiking wildly and keeps the patient consistently comfortable. Simple and effective nursing care!

question: A nurse notices pressure sores are common in the elderly ward and tries a new turning schedule. What is this an example of?

options.A: An illegal medical experiment on vulnerable human subjects
options.B: A quality improvement project based on clinical observation
options.C: A violation of hospital administrative policy
options.D: A financial investment in medical equipment manufacturing

explanation: Spot on! Noticing a ward problem and trying a practical nursing fix to make things better is a classic quality improvement project.

question: What technology does an autoclave use to sterilize medical instruments and waste?

options.A: Pressurized steam
options.B: Dry microwave heat
options.C: Freezing temperatures
options.D: Ultraviolet rays

explanation: Autoclaves use high heat and pressure generated by steam to destroy all microbial life on equipment. [learn more](GST114_U2_T14#GST114_U2_T14_h5)

question: How do strong social support systems help protect a person's mental health?

options.A: They eliminate all stressful events from happening in life
options.B: They ensure the person never experiences sadness
options.C: They replace the need for professional psychiatric medication
options.D: They provide emotional validation and practical help during crises

explanation: Having friends or family who listen and stand by you makes heavy burdens feel much lighter.

question: Why must you always lock your computer screen when walking away from the nurses' station?

options.A: To prevent the central processing unit from overheating during idle times
options.B: To automatically save any unsaved nursing notes to the cloud
options.C: To save electrical power and extend the lifespan of the monitor display
options.D: To protect patient privacy and prevent unauthorized access to health records

question: Which of these conditions is best suited for ongoing tele-nursing management?

options.A: Acute traumatic limb amputation
options.B: Emergency cardiac arrest
options.C: Hypertension and diabetes
options.D: Sudden severe appendicitis

explanation: Correct! Chronic illnesses that need daily lifestyle support and regular checks are perfect candidates for virtual follow-ups.

question: Which sign is a classic giveaway of an opioid overdose?

options.A: Pinpoint pupils
options.B: Extreme pupil dilation
options.C: Uncontrollable muscle tremors
options.D: Severe skin redness and sweating

explanation: Spot on! Tiny, pinpoint pupils combined with slow breathing are classic red flags for opioid overdose.

question: A patient lacks a specific nutrient in their diet and shows deficiency signs, but labs show their body can easily make similar compounds. What kind of nutrient is this?

options.A: Inorganic mineral
options.B: Essential nutrient
options.C: Inert fiber
options.D: Non-essential nutrient

explanation: If the body can synthesize it independently, it's considered non-essential because we don't strictly have to get it directly from our meals.

question: Why is consistency in applying discipline legally important for a manager?

options.A: It allows the manager to skip documenting incidents
options.B: It guarantees that no employee will ever make a mistake
options.C: It eliminates the need for progressive steps
options.D: It prevents claims of discrimination and unfair treatment

explanation: Treating different staff members fairly and equally protects the organization against legal charges of bias. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h7)

question: Why did people in early history practice family planning?

options.A: To increase the speed of urban industrial growth
options.B: To comply with modern hospital guidelines
options.C: To eliminate the need for traditional birth attendants
options.D: To manage family size and resource allocation

explanation: Even long ago, communities needed to make sure they had enough food and resources for everyone, so they practiced family planning to manage family size.

question: In clinical communication, what does the acronym SBAR stand for?

options.A: System, Behavior, Analysis, Response
options.B: Symptoms, Blood, Airways, Respiration
options.C: Safety, Balance, Action, Review
options.D: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation

explanation: SBAR is a handy, structured tool nurses and doctors use to pass clear patient updates across quickly and safely.

question: Which of these is a bad practice when looking at clinical data?

options.A: Looking at trends over several months instead of one week
options.B: Ignoring the denominator when looking at small sample sizes
options.C: Reviewing how patient data was collected in the first place
options.D: Checking whether two events are truly related before acting

explanation: Well done! Forgetting the total number of patients can make a tiny issue look like a massive epidemic. Always check the whole picture!

question: What is the very first step a nurse should take when entering a new community for health mobilisation?

options.A: Administering vaccines without telling anyone first
options.B: Visiting local leaders to gain entry and approval
options.C: Building a clinic fence using community donations
options.D: Conducting a written examination for all adults

explanation: Community entry respects local hierarchy and customs by seeking permission and blessing from traditional or civic authorities first. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why is system integration important for hospital technology tools?

options.A: It lowers the physical weight of computer monitors at the nursing station
options.B: It removes the need for any internet connection in the hospital
options.C: It allows separate digital tools to share data and work together smoothly
options.D: It forces all patients to use mobile phones for their medical records

explanation: Integration connects isolated systems so information flows freely between inventory, staffing, and patient care records. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h5)

question: Which of these is a non-pharmacological comfort measure a nurse can use during a disaster?

options.A: Intravenous morphine administration
options.B: Emergency surgical airway placement
options.C: Rapid blood transfusion
options.D: Gentle repositioning and reassuring communication

explanation: Spot on! Non-pharmacological means soothing the patient without drugs—using your nursing touch, kind words, and proper positioning to ease their distress.

question: How do clinical decision support systems help protect patients from medication errors?

options.A: By automatically administering pills without nurse verification
options.B: By completely eliminating the need for doctors to write prescriptions
options.C: By locking the pharmacy storage room during night shifts
options.D: By alerting nurses to potential drug interactions or wrong dosages

explanation: Decision support tools use programmed rules to warn clinicians about safety issues like dangerous drug interactions before a mistake happens. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h5)

question: When must a pair of disposable medical gloves be changed?

options.A: Only when they show visible tears
options.B: Before washing your hands
options.C: Between caring for different patients
options.D: At the end of an eight-hour shift

explanation: Gloves must always be changed between patients to prevent carrying micro-organisms from one person to another. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h3)

question: How should you document an adverse event in the patient's clinical chart?

options.A: Include notes about the hospital management being careless
options.B: Record objective clinical findings and nursing interventions clearly
options.C: Write down personal opinions about which coworker made the mistake
options.D: Avoid mentioning the event entirely to prevent patient anxiety

explanation: Keep your charting strictly factual! Write down only what you see, assess, and do for the patient.

question: What is the main difference between proactive and reactive risk strategies?

options.A: Proactive strategies cost more money than any reactive hospital investigation
options.B: Proactive strategies are handled by doctors, while reactive strategies are handled by nurses
options.C: Proactive strategies act before harm happens, while reactive strategies respond after harm occurs
options.D: Proactive strategies focus on equipment, while reactive strategies focus on staff

explanation: The timing is the key difference: stopping an accident beforehand versus cleaning up the pieces after an accident takes place. [learn more](GST319_U4_T6#GST319_U4_T6_h4)

question: Why shouldn't you pour leftover liquid medicines down a regular sink drain?

options.A: It causes immediate blockages in iron plumbing pipes
options.B: It pollutes local water sources and the environment
options.C: It reacts violently with ordinary soap and water
options.D: It produces toxic gases inside the nursing station

question: Why is a quick review session important right after finishing a community disaster simulation?

options.A: To identify weaknesses in the plan and discuss areas for improvement
options.B: To officially close down the community health center for repairs
options.C: To fine community members who moved too slowly
options.D: To hand out formal employment contracts to volunteers

explanation: Spot on! Reviewing the drill helps organizers and participants spot problems and fix safety gaps before a real disaster happens.

question: What is the main goal of having both the sympathetic and parasympathetic systems working together?

options.A: Maintaining a stable internal body balance
options.B: Preventing the brain from ever sleeping
options.C: Keeping the heart rate as high as possible
options.D: Ensuring constant physical exhaustion

explanation: Both systems balance each other out to achieve homeostasis—a fancy word for keeping your internal body happy, stable, and healthy. Brilliant work!

question: In research terms, how does a 'sample' connect to a 'population'?

options.A: The sample is a smaller, manageable subset chosen to represent the broader population
options.B: The population and the sample must always contain the exact same number of people
options.C: The sample includes every single individual who has ever had the medical condition
options.D: The population is just a pilot group tested before the main sample is selected

explanation: You got it! We study the smaller group (the sample) so we can figure out what is happening in the big group (the population) without getting overwhelmed.

question: Which part of the chain of infection does contact tracing target the most?

options.A: Infectious agent mutation
options.B: Host genetic susceptibility
options.C: Reservoir sanitization
options.D: Mode of transmission

explanation: You've got this! By finding exposed contacts and keeping them away from others, we block the germ from moving from one person to another.

question: A patient has an open fracture with a small piece of bone sticking out of the skin. What is the correct initial nursing action?

options.A: Wash the exposed bone vigorously with strong antiseptic soap and water
options.B: Straighten the limb forcefully to hide the bone before taking an X-ray

options.D: Cover the wound loosely with a sterile dressing without pushing the bone in

question: Why should a nurse study local disease patterns before planning a health talk?

explanation: Well done! Every community is unique. Knowing their specific challenges helps you focus on what actually matters to them.

question: What is the greatest superpower of using a mixed methods design in nursing?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any statistical software programs
options.B: It provides a more complete and thorough picture of a clinical problem
options.C: It is always cheaper and faster to execute than other designs
options.D: It completely removes all forms of bias from the study

explanation: Spot on! By combining hard numbers with real human experiences, you get a much richer understanding of a health issue.

question: A nurse checks a client's chart to see if their symptoms have lasted long enough to meet clinical guidelines. Which manual is she likely using?

options.A: The DSM-5-TR

options.C: The Hospital Safety Manual
options.D: The British Pharmacopoeia

question: Which of these is a common way gender bias shows up in clinical care?

options.A: Children being denied vaccines based on their biological sex
options.B: Men receiving lower doses of routine prescription antibiotics

question: Which of these is a common traditional explanation often given for mental illness?

options.A: Regular physical exercise routines
options.B: A balanced and nutritious diet

options.D: Spiritual attacks and witchcraft

question: What is the main function of a computerized staffing system?

options.A: To calculate the exact financial salary of every hospital worker

options.D: To generate balanced work schedules based on patient needs and staff skills

question: A nurse ignores a ward medication rule, and the patient gets hurt. What legal problem might this cause?

options.A: The hospital policy automatically protects the nurse from blame
options.B: The legal system ignores internal hospital rules completely

question: What is the main goal of disease surveillance at local health centers during an outbreak?

options.A: To treat water supply dams with heavy chemical disinfectants

question: What is the primary goal of Primary Health Care (PHC) in a community?

question: What happens to the mother's heart output right after the placenta is delivered?

question: Why does public stigma surrounding mental illness often hurt patients?

question: What are the three core parts of the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Infection, morbidity, and mortality

question: What does de-identifying a dataset involve?

question: How does a community nurse act as a bridge for families?

question: Why do babies with sickle cell anaemia usually look completely healthy at birth?

options.A: The bone marrow does not produce red blood cells until the age of one

question: What is the name of the hollow ball of cells that gets ready to implant in the uterus?

question: How is prevalence different from incidence?

options.D: Prevalence ignores people who are currently receiving care

question: What does the clinical communication shortcut SBAR stand for?

options.D: Symptoms, Behavior, Action, Response

question: What is the main function of the aggregation stage in the supply chain?

question: Which clinical setting uses an ambulatory EHR system?

question: What does human factors engineering mainly look at in a hospital setting?

question: Why are sharps containers made with hard, thick plastic walls?

question: A patient arrives at your clinic with a long-term cough, heavy night sweats, and sudden weight loss. What should you do first?

options.B: Scheduling an immediate abdominal ultrasound

question: Why is good nutrition and protein especially vital for patients healing from deep wounds like pressure sores?

options.A: Cells need building blocks to repair the extracellular matrix and regenerate tissue

options.C: Vitamins automatically clean bacteria out of closed body cavities

question: Which tiny structures in the upper dermis are responsible for giving you your unique fingerprints?

options.A: Elastic fibers
options.B: Sweat glands
options.C: Dermal papillae
options.D: Subcutaneous fat

question: What does indirect calorimetry measure to calculate energy use?

options.A: Urinary nitrogen and fluid loss
options.B: Total body heat in a sealed room
options.C: Oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production

question: What is the main reason hospitals conduct pre-employment health checks for new nursing staff?

options.A: To establish a baseline health status and ensure fitness for the job
options.B: To lower the hospital's monthly utility and supply expenses
options.C: To test the worker's knowledge of medical terminology

question: What was the early nature of psychiatric facilities like the Yaba Lunatic Asylum when first opened?

options.A: Private luxury retreats for wealthy politicians

options.C: Advanced community wellness centers with modern psychotherapy

question: What does a risk assessment mainly look at?

options.A: The speed at which emergency vehicles can travel
options.B: The exact budget needed to rebuild a damaged clinic
options.C: The likelihood of a hazard and population vulnerability
options.D: The personal medical history of disaster survivors

question: Why is good etiquette especially important when nursing inside a patient's home?

options.A: It replaces the need for actual clinical skills and assessments
options.B: It ensures the family will buy extra medical supplies for the patient
options.C: It helps the nurse balance being a polite guest with upholding professional standards

question: Why are IPC rules still enforced in a quarantine zone where people feel healthy?

options.A: To test the durability of hospital cleaning supplies

question: A menopausal patient has vaginal spotting and mild burning. What is the most likely cause of her cervical sensitivity?

question: What was the main focus of early psychoanalytic therapy?

options.A: Isolating patients from stressful family environments
options.B: Training patients to change bad habits through rewards
options.C: Exploring hidden conflicts in the unconscious mind
options.D: Using electrical shocks to reset brain chemistry

question: Why might giving iron tablets fail to cure a patient's anemia if underlying food taboos are ignored?

options.B: Iron tablets are completely useless against traditional beliefs

options.D: Supplements make the patient develop an instant allergy to vegetables

explanation: Pills alone won't fix a problem driven by daily diet. If the patient is still culturally banned from eating iron-rich foods, the deficiency will just keep coming back.

question: A clinic is starting a digital triage system but keeps paper registers nearby just in case the network goes down. What is this strategy called?

options.A: Outcome measurement
options.B: Stakeholder engagement
options.C: Risk mitigation
options.D: Aim setting

explanation: You've got this! Having a reliable backup plan for when things go wrong (like poor internet or power cuts) is called risk mitigation.

question: A patient with heart failure repeatedly misses their diuretic medication. What is this patient most likely to experience?

options.A: Severe fluid overload and breathing difficulties
options.B: Lowered blood pressure to normal limits
options.C: Complete recovery from heart muscle weakness
options.D: Rapid weight loss and extreme dehydration

explanation: Diuretics help the body get rid of excess fluid; missing them allows fluid to back up into the lungs, causing severe shortness of breath. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h3)

question: When checking a patient with dark skin for inflammation, what should you look out for?

options.A: Dark brown, purplish, or grey discoloration instead of bright redness
options.B: Bright cherry-red patches that are easily visible on all skin types
options.C: Neon yellow borders surrounding every single affected skin plaque
options.D: A complete absence of any color change with only flaking present

explanation: Great clinical eye! On darker skin tones, inflammation often shows up as deeper brown, purple, or grey shades rather than standard red.

question: On a scatter diagram, what does a single dot represent?

options.A: The total average of all patients in the study
options.B: The error rate of the measuring instrument
options.C: The difference between two hospital wards
options.D: One subject's values for both variables combined

explanation: Each dot is like a snapshot for one individual participant, showing both of their measurements meeting at a point.

question: Which of the following is NOT a core characteristic of a good healthcare plan?

options.A: Simplicity
options.B: Flexibility
options.C: Feasibility
options.D: Rigidity

explanation: Good plans must bend and adapt, so rigidity makes a plan fail when unexpected clinical situations arise. [learn more](GST321_U1_T7#GST321_U1_T7_h2)

question: Why is it so important to build quick rapport with a patient right at the start of an interview?

options.A: It prevents the patient from asking any difficult questions
options.B: It shortens the total time needed for the physical exam
options.C: It guarantees the patient will follow all medication orders
options.D: It lowers patient anxiety and encourages honest sharing

explanation: Exactly! When patients feel safe and respected by you, they relax and open up about what is truly bothering them.

question: What two main fields are combined to create nursing informatics?

options.A: Biology and hospital administration
options.B: Nursing science and computer science
options.C: Pharmacology and engineering
options.D: Medicine and data entry

explanation: Nursing informatics specifically blends nursing science with information and computer sciences to manage healthcare data effectively. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which group of medical parasites is made up of tiny, single-celled organisms?

options.A: Nematodes
options.B: Cestodes
options.C: Protozoa
options.D: Helminths

explanation: Think 'proto' as in primitive or single. Protozoa are microscopic, single-celled fighters that can multiply super fast inside you.

question: What are small pieces of digital data called when they travel across a network?

options.A: Pixels
options.B: Packets
options.C: Pulses
options.D: Plugs

explanation: Data is broken down into small units known as packets so it can travel efficiently across computer networks. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h2)

question: Which everyday activity is most likely to trigger sharp pain in a pregnant woman with relaxed pelvic joints?

options.A: Deep breathing exercises while sitting upright
options.B: Chewing hard foods during breakfast
options.C: Writing notes with a heavy pen
options.D: Stepping out of a car with one leg at a time

explanation: Movements that involve stepping out sideways or widening the legs unevenly—like getting out of a car—put extra strain on relaxed pelvic joints.

question: Which special pathways let electrical signals pass straight from one heart cell to the next?

options.A: Gap junctions
options.B: T-tubules
options.C: Sarcoplasmic reticula
options.D: Desmosomes

explanation: Gap junctions act like open doors (or tunnels) that let electrical signals zoom quickly between neighbor cells, keeping your heartbeat coordinated.

question: Which food combination is strictly forbidden under traditional Jewish kosher laws?

options.A: Fresh fruits and chicken broth
options.B: Meat and dairy products eaten together
options.C: Fish with scales and cooked vegetables
options.D: Cattle meat and whole wheat bread

explanation: Kosher law keeps meat and dairy completely separate—they cannot be cooked or eaten in the same meal, and separate kitchen utensils are often used!

question: If a student wants to study how hospital room ventilation and fresh air affect patient healing, which theory fits best?

options.A: Callista Roy’s Adaptation Model
options.B: Dorothea Orem’s Self-Care Deficit Theory
options.C: Florence Nightingale’s Environmental Theory
options.D: Madeleine Leininger’s Culture Care Theory

explanation: You nailed it! Nightingale was the pioneer of using clean air, light, and a healthy environment to help patients recover.

question: What factor can significantly alter a child's vital sign readings during a home assessment?

options.A: The time of the family meal
options.B: The brand of soap used at home
options.C: Crying or anxiety
options.D: The color of the bedroom wall

explanation: Correct! Fear, anxiety, or crying can cause a child's heart rate and breathing to jump up temporarily. Always keep that in mind during assessments! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T11#GNS324_U3_T11_h3)

question: Which part of the brain is the main control center for processing fear and triggering our fight-or-flight alarm?

options.A: Medulla oblongata
options.B: Cerebellum
options.C: Amygdala
options.D: Pituitary gland

explanation: Think of the amygdala as your brain's emotional smoke detector. It spots danger and sounds the alarm right away!

question: Why is it important for a nurse to respect local food taboos rather than arguing with patients about them?

options.A: To build trust and encourage open communication with patients
options.B: To ensure the hospital saves money on meals
options.C: To follow strict government nursing regulations
options.D: To prove that traditional beliefs are always scientifically correct

explanation: When we respect our patients' beliefs instead of judging them, they feel safe and are more likely to share their real health habits with us. Great nursing is all about connection!

question: Which side effect tends to happen with almost all oral antiparasitic medications?

options.A: Sudden yellowing of the skin and sclera
options.B: Gastrointestinal upset like nausea and cramps
options.C: Severe hair loss within the first week
options.D: Permanent hearing loss in high frequencies

explanation: Most oral antiparasitic drugs are a bit rough on the stomach lining, often leading to mild nausea, stomach cramps, or tummy discomfort.

question: What is the most important infection control practice for a family caregiver managing a home gastrostomy tube?

options.A: Boiling all feeding bags in water after every single meal
options.B: Performing thorough hand hygiene before handling the tube
options.C: Cleaning the entire feeding pump machine with bleach daily
options.D: Wearing sterile surgical gloves for every single water flush

explanation: Proper handwashing is the single most effective way to prevent harmful bacteria from entering the gastrostomy site or formula bag. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of a research design in nursing?

options.A: To calculate the final cost of the research project
options.B: To replace the need for an institutional review board
options.C: To format the bibliography of a research paper
options.D: To act as a blueprint for answering a clinical question

explanation: Think of a research design like an architectural blueprint. It gives you a clear, step-by-step plan to follow so you can find accurate answers to your clinical questions!

question: Why is connecting families to local respite care services important?

options.A: It replaces the need for professional nursing visits entirely.
options.B: It prevents caregiver burnout and supports long-term caregiving.
options.C: It permanently removes the child from the parents' custody.
options.D: It ensures that parents never have to administer medications again.

explanation: You got it! Caring for a sick child is exhausting work, and respite care gives parents a well-deserved break to rest and recharge. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T11#GNS324_U3_T11_h8)

question: Why is manually copying patient data dangerous in a clinical setting?

options.A: It automatically deletes vital sign history from the computer
options.B: It prevents the pharmacy from ever dispensing any drugs
options.C: It causes the hospital internet network to crash completely
options.D: It increases the risk of transcription errors and delays

explanation: Spotting mistakes is key to safe nursing! Copying things by hand takes extra time and opens the door to human errors that could affect patient safety. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which inner layer of the joint capsule is responsible for making synovial fluid?

options.A: The outer reinforcing ligament band
options.B: The outer fibrous capsule layer
options.C: The glassy articular cartilage pad
options.D: The inner synovial membrane

explanation: Brilliant! The inner lining is the synovial membrane—it acts like a little factory that secretes that slippery fluid.

question: Which tool helps a patient who struggles to bend down to wash their lower legs and feet?

options.A: A long-handled sponge
options.B: A mechanical hoist
options.C: A standard walking frame
options.D: A raised toilet seat

explanation: Brilliant! A long-handled sponge is a simple yet clever device that lets patients reach their feet easily without straining their backs.

question: What makes an abortion procedure classified as "unsafe"?

options.A: An elective termination performed using modern pharmaceutical drugs
options.B: Any pregnancy loss occurring naturally during the first trimester
options.C: A legal surgical procedure performed by a certified gynecologist
options.D: A termination done without proper medical training or in unsterile settings

explanation: You've got this! An unsafe abortion simply means it was carried out by untrained hands or in dirty places, which puts the patient at a huge risk for severe complications. Spotting this definition helps you protect your patients early!

question: Which stage of the schistosome life cycle can directly infect humans?

options.A: Sporocysts
options.B: Miracidia
options.C: Cercariae
options.D: Eggs

explanation: Cercariae are the free-swimming little swimmers released by snails into the water. When they touch human skin, they dive right in! You've got this.

question: Why must you be extra careful when trying to use the basilic vein for venepuncture?

options.A: It lies close to the brachial artery and median nerve
options.B: It carries oxygenated blood directly from the lungs
options.C: It is too small to yield an adequate blood sample
options.D: It has thick muscular walls that resist needle entry

explanation: Be cautious with the basilic vein—major nerves and the brachial artery run right beside it, so care is needed to avoid accidental injury.

question: Which of the following is a common long-term side effect of taking corticosteroids?

options.A: Permanently low blood pressure
options.B: Darkening of the skin tone
options.C: Rapid muscle building and weight loss
options.D: Osteoporosis and weak bones

explanation: Correct! Long-term steroid use messes with calcium and bone building, which can lead to fragile bones over time. Good clinical knowledge!

question: Why can't a nurse officially diagnose a patient with diabetes based on just one high random blood sugar test?

options.A: Glucometers cannot measure glucose above 150 mg/dL
options.B: Blood sugar levels never stay high for long periods
options.C: It is a screening test and needs confirmatory tests
options.D: Only laboratory nurses are allowed to make a diagnosis

explanation: Meals, stress, and illness can cause temporary spikes. Doctors rely on fasting tests or HbA1c to make a formal diagnosis.

question: A hospital management wants to check if nurses are keeping proper wound care records. What should they do?

options.A: Increasing the number of night shifts for junior nurses
options.B: Transferring patients with wounds to a different facility
options.C: Organizing a social party for all the nursing staff
options.D: Conducting a nursing audit of surgical ward case notes

explanation: Exactly! Reviewing actual clinical charts through an audit gives clear proof of how well wound care is being documented and performed.

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge to getting accurate data on a busy ward?

options.A: Excessive availability of fully automated digital tools
options.B: Incomplete record-keeping in traditional paper registers
options.C: Heavy workloads and severe shortages of nursing personnel
options.D: Fear of punishment among staff when reporting clinical errors

explanation: We wish we had too much tech! In reality, staff shortages, paper logs, and fear of getting in trouble are the real hurdles—not having an overload of digital tools.

question: What is the main thing a nurse does when acting as a health advocate?

options.A: Diagnosing complex medical conditions independently
options.B: Prescribing emergency medications during shortages
options.C: Speaking up for patients and protecting their rights
options.D: Managing the financial budget of the health facility

explanation: You got this! Being a health advocate simply means standing up for your patients, defending their rights, and helping them navigate the healthcare system.

question: Which of these factors generally improves the long-term outlook for a child with a behaviour disorder?

options.A: Timely and consistent therapeutic intervention
options.B: Waiting until adulthood for natural maturity
options.C: Avoiding all contact with mental health professionals
options.D: Changing schools every single year

explanation: Early, structured support from healthcare providers and family gives the child much better coping skills for a bright future!

question: What symptom of chronic mental illness is structured work especially good at helping?

options.A: Sudden bone fractures and sprains
options.B: Severe vitamin deficiency states
options.C: Apathy and social withdrawal
options.D: Acute high fever and body chills

explanation: Having regular daily tasks and meeting peers helps pull clients out of isolation and inactivity. Every question brings you closer to clinical success!

question: What is the main difference between latent TB and active TB disease?

options.A: Latent TB bacteria are dead, while active TB bacteria are alive.
options.B: Latent TB requires hospital admission, while active TB is treated at home.
options.C: Latent TB only affects children, while active TB only affects adults.
options.D: Latent TB has no symptoms and is not contagious, whereas active TB causes illness and spreads.

explanation: Think of latent TB as sleeping quietly in the body—the person feels fine and cannot pass it on. Active TB is awake, causing illness, and can spread to others.

question: How can bedside nurses directly help with hospital financial efficiency?

options.A: By collecting taxes from patients at the hospital gate
options.B: By preventing waste of medical supplies and reducing patient complications
options.C: By negotiating insurance premium rates directly with corporate bosses
options.D: By deciding the annual national health budget in Parliament

explanation: As a nurse, being careful with consumables and preventing infections (like bedsores) means patients heal faster and use fewer resources—saving everyone money!

question: What does social inclusion mean for a person living with a physical disability?

options.A: Depending entirely on family members for all daily social interactions
options.B: Living exclusively in specialized care facilities with other disabled peers
options.C: Having equal opportunities to work, learn, and participate in community life
options.D: Avoiding public spaces to prevent unwanted attention from strangers

explanation: Social inclusion ensures full participation in society, including employment, education, voting, and recreation. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h8)

question: Which skin change is a classic sign of chronic primary adrenal insufficiency, also known as Addison's disease?

options.A: Flushing
options.B: Hyperpigmentation
options.C: Jaundice
options.D: Cyanosis

explanation: In Addison's disease, low cortisol makes the brain pump out extra ACTH, which accidentally darkens the skin, especially over knuckles and pressure points. It's a classic clinical clue!

question: What is a main difference between personal and organisational objectives?

options.A: Personal goals focus on individual growth, while organisational goals focus on collective institutional success
options.B: Personal goals never involve learning or professional development
options.C: Personal goals are always written by the government, while organisational goals are written by nurses
options.D: Organisational goals only care about individual staff salaries

explanation: Think of it simply: personal goals are about your own growth and pocket, while organisational goals are about the success and health standards of the whole hospital.

question: Which of the following is NOT helpful to include when charting about a patient's cough?

options.A: Factors that make the coughing worse
options.B: The color and amount of any sputum produced
options.C: The brand of soap used in the hospital room
options.D: Whether the cough is dry or productive

explanation: You got it! The soap brand won't change lung assessment findings, but details about sputum, triggers, and cough type are clinical gold!

question: What is the trick to using a penlight sideways (tangential lighting) during a skin check?

options.A: To cast shadows that highlight the elevation or depression of a skin lesion
options.B: To sterilize the immediate area surrounding an open wound
options.C: To measure the exact surface area diameter of a chronic skin ulcer
options.D: To warm up cold skin before checking the patient's overall turgor

explanation: Shining the light from the side creates helpful shadows. This makes bumps, lumps, or dents much easier to spot!

question: How do tables and bullet points help when writing clinical documents?

options.A: They encrypt the document to prevent unauthorized access
options.B: They remove the need for grammar and spelling checks
options.C: They make complex medical information clean and readable
options.D: They automatically convert text into numerical clinical data

explanation: Great formatting is a lifesaver! Breaking down heavy medical text with bullet points helps busy nurses find important details in a flash. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h2)

question: A patient with diabetes mellitus develops peripheral neuropathy. Which symptom would you most expect to see?

options.A: Instant spastic paralysis of both upper extremities
options.B: Rapid increase in cognitive processing speed
options.C: Loss of voluntary control over heart contractions
options.D: Numbness and loss of protective sensation in the feet

explanation: Peripheral neuropathy frequently robs patients of sensation in their hands and feet, which is why daily foot checks are so crucial in nursing care for diabetics!

question: Which of these activities is a great example of 'mutual aid'?

options.A: Neighbors contributing money to pay for a sick person's hospital bill
options.B: A police officer giving a traffic ticket to a speeding driver
options.C: A commercial bank approving a business loan for a farmer
options.D: A teacher giving a graded examination to students in a school

explanation: Spot on! Mutual aid happens when community members voluntarily join hands to support someone who is sick or in need.

question: A patient loves the extra sympathy and gets excused from chores because of physical complaints that doctors can't find a medical cause for. What is this called?

options.A: Primary gain
options.B: Secondary gain
options.C: Cognitive dissonance
options.D: Neuroplasticity

explanation: Spot on! Secondary gain refers to the external perks—like extra care, sympathy, or getting out of house chores—that come along with playing the sick role.

question: Which of these bones develops directly through intramembranous ossification?

options.A: Tibia of the lower leg
options.B: Humerus of the upper arm
options.C: Femur of the thigh
options.D: Flat bones of the skull

explanation: Great job! Flat bones (like your skull and jaw) form directly from sheets of tissue without needing a cartilage model first.

question: Why does relaxing the muscle around the airways make breathing easier?

options.A: It increases airway radius and lowers resistance to airflow
options.B: It stops the lungs from producing excess fluid
options.C: It completely cures chronic lung inflammation
options.D: It strengthens the diaphragm muscle during inhalation

explanation: Think of a garden hose: when you relax a tight squeeze, the pipe opens up and water flows smoothly. It's the same idea for air flowing into the lungs!

question: Which simple device is used to check how fast a patient can forcefully blow air out of their lungs?

options.A: Sphygmomanometer
options.B: Peak flow meter
options.C: Otoscope
options.D: Pulse oximeter

explanation: Spot on! A peak flow meter is a handy little tool nurses use to keep an eye on airflow in asthma patients.

question: Which practice helps prevent visual eavesdropping on patient electronic health records in a busy ward?

options.A: Leaving workstation sessions logged in overnight for easy access
options.B: Writing patient passwords on sticky notes attached to the monitor
options.C: Positioning computer screens away from public view and hallways
options.D: Using large font sizes so visitors can read updates from afar

explanation: Shielding monitors from visitors and passersby stops unauthorized people from reading sensitive clinical data on screen. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is often one of the very first warning signs of internal cancers like stomach or pancreatic cancer?

options.A: Unexplained weight loss
options.B: High fever and chills
options.C: Severe joint swelling
options.D: Sudden visual impairment

explanation: When growing tumors change the body's metabolism and steal nutrients, rapid, unexpected weight loss can happen. Good clinical awareness!

question: What does the letter 'E' stand for in the health acronym IEC?

options.A: Evaluation
options.B: Environment
options.C: Education
options.D: Emergency

explanation: IEC stands for Information, Education, and Communication, which are core components of public health promotion strategies. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T4#GNS124_U5_T4_h1)

question: What kind of immunity does a baby get when receiving antibodies through breast milk?

options.A: Natural active immunity
options.B: Artificial active immunity
options.C: Artificial passive immunity
options.D: Natural passive immunity

explanation: Spot on! Because the baby receives ready-made antibodies naturally from the mother, it's natural passive immunity.

question: Why shouldn't a nurse rely only on visual physical checks when diagnosing malnutrition?

options.A: Clinical signs only appear after the patient is completely cured
options.B: Laboratory tests are illegal to perform in primary health clinics
options.C: Different nutrient shortages can cause very similar physical signs
options.D: Patients usually hide their physical symptoms from healthcare workers

explanation: Many deficiencies look alike on the outside. That's why we always back up our physical exams with diet histories and lab tests!

question: Why do we call patient assessment in the intensive care unit a continuous loop?

options.A: Because vital signs never change in stable patients
options.B: Because doctors only visit patients once a day
options.C: Because hospital computers demand hourly data entry
options.D: Because interventions require constant re-evaluation

explanation: Think of it as a cycle: you assess, you act, and then you immediately check how the patient responded. It keeps repeating to keep them safe!

question: A stroke patient has weak muscles and needs a little bit of help to move their arm fully. What exercise is best?

options.A: Active-assistive exercises
options.B: Passive range of motion
options.C: Complete bed rest restriction
options.D: Heavy weightlifting resistance

explanation: Teamwork! The patient does as much as they can, and you help finish the movement. That is active-assistive exercise.

question: How does a hormonal IUD locally affect the uterus to help prevent pregnancy?

options.A: It dilates the cervix to flush out incoming sperm
options.B: It stretches the muscle fibers to cause cramping
options.C: It secretes an enzyme that destroys ovarian follicles
options.D: It thins the endometrial lining significantly

explanation: The local release of progestin keeps the uterine lining nice and thin, making it impossible for a fertilized egg to plant itself.

question: A nurse notices a toddler has not started walking or babbling by the expected age. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.A: Tell the parents to wait until the child turns five years old
options.B: Discontinue all routine immunizations immediately
options.C: Refer the child for formal developmental screening and evaluation
options.D: Prescribe broad-spectrum antibiotics for a suspected infection

explanation: Missed milestones should prompt formal screening to catch potential delays early and start interventions. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h2)

question: Why can extreme heat exposure during early pregnancy be risky for the developing baby?

options.A: It instantly changes the genetic blood type of the fetus
options.B: It triggers early puberty inside the womb
options.C: It causes the placenta to detach immediately on the first day
options.D: It can interfere with proper implantation and increase the risk of miscarriage

explanation: During early pregnancy, cells are dividing rapidly. High heat can disrupt this delicate process and put the pregnancy at risk. Every bit of knowledge gets you closer to exam success!

question: What is the primary action of vasopressor medications like norepinephrine in shock?

options.A: Dissolve blood clots in the coronary arteries
options.B: Dilate the bronchial tubes in the lungs
options.C: Slow down a rapid heart rate
options.D: Constrict blood vessels to raise blood pressure

explanation: Vasopressors cause blood vessels to tighten, which increases vascular resistance and helps raise blood pressure when fluids are not enough. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h6)

question: Why is taking a good patient history considered the bedrock of your clinical nursing practice?

options.A: It provides definitive proof of a medical diagnosis
options.B: It replaces the need for any laboratory investigations
options.C: It guides your physical assessment and care planning
options.D: It eliminates all risks of clinical documentation errors

explanation: Spot on! A thorough history points you in the right direction, helping you know where to focus your physical exam and how to plan the best care.

question: What is the primary risk of contaminating a microbiological specimen with normal skin flora?

options.A: It causes the laboratory equipment to short circuit
options.B: It leads to false-positive results and inappropriate treatment
options.C: It permanently ruins the patient's blood pressure record
options.D: It speeds up the natural healing rate of the surgical wound

explanation: Skin germs growing in the lab can trick doctors into treating harmless bacteria instead of the true infection. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h5)

question: What does hyperreflexia during a neurological exam usually point to?

options.A: Complete destruction of the sensory receptors in the skin
options.B: A lower motor neuron injury affecting peripheral nerves
options.C: An upper motor neuron lesion in the brain or spinal cord
options.D: Severe dehydration leading to temporary muscle cramps

explanation: Normally, the brain keeps our reflexes in check. When upper motor neurons are damaged, that control is lost, making reflexes overly jumpy (hyperreflexia).

question: Which important vitamin is made by the friendly bacteria living in your large intestine?

options.A: Vitamin C
options.B: Vitamin K
options.C: Vitamin A
options.D: Vitamin D

explanation: Your gut bacteria are tiny vitamin factories! They produce Vitamin K, which is super important for helping your blood clot properly.

question: Which of these is NOT a standard reason for routine lab testing in dairy production?

options.A: Checking for excessive bacterial load in raw milk supplies
options.B: Guaranteeing that the milk contains zero water molecules
options.C: Confirming the success of the pasteurization process
options.D: Verifying the overall sanitation of milking equipment

explanation: Spot on! Microbiological tests look for bacteria and check if pasteurization worked. Water content is measured separately using physics methods like cryoscopy, not germ tests!

question: What is the best way to write down a patient's chief complaint in their clinical chart?

options.A: Use the patient's own words inside quotation marks
options.B: Translate their description into complex medical jargon
options.C: Leave the exact wording out and just write your diagnosis
options.D: Summarize what you think they meant in your own words

explanation: Correct! Putting their exact words in quotes keeps their story pure without adding your own guesswork.

question: A researcher wants to show how blood pressure readings changed across four different clinic visits for a group of patients. Which format should they choose?

options.A: A graph
options.B: A qualitative interview transcript
options.C: A dense text paragraph
options.D: A demographic listing

explanation: Graphs are the best format for illustrating trends and changes across multiple time points, like clinic visits. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T4#GNS224_U2_T4_h2)

question: Why do healthy pregnant women need to produce more insulin as their pregnancy advances?

options.A: The growing fetus directly destroys maternal pancreatic cells
options.B: The liver stores less glucose as pregnancy progresses
options.C: Placental hormones make maternal cells more resistant to insulin
options.D: Maternal kidneys begin to excrete insulin much faster

explanation: As the placenta grows, it releases hormones that create insulin resistance, forcing the pancreas to pump out extra insulin to keep blood sugar stable. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h1)

question: What happens in a negative correlation between two variables?

options.A: As one variable increases, the other variable decreases
options.B: Both variables decrease at the exact same time
options.C: Both variables increase at the exact same time
options.D: There is no relationship found between the variables

explanation: Think of it like a seesaw: in a negative correlation, as one variable goes up, the other goes down. Great job thinking it through!

question: What is the difference between a key driver and a change idea?

options.A: Drivers deal only with financial costs, while change ideas deal with clinical medications
options.B: Drivers are primary systems influencing the outcome, while change ideas are specific practical actions to test
options.C: Drivers are chosen by hospital directors, while change ideas are chosen by patients
options.D: Drivers are written on paper, while change ideas are only spoken aloud

explanation: Think of drivers as the big areas we need to influence, while change ideas are the fun, practical steps we actually try out on the ward!

question: Why is educational informatics particularly useful when clinical placement sites are scarce?

options.A: It automates the grading of physical bedside nursing procedures
options.B: It provides virtual patient scenarios to practice clinical reasoning
options.C: It allows students to skip graduation exams and start working early
options.D: It completely replaces the need for licensed nursing faculty

explanation: Simulation and virtual tools give students valuable practice in decision-making when real clinical wards are overcrowded. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T2#GNS113_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why is it important to monitor pressure and volume during mechanical ventilation?

options.A: It controls the exact body temperature of the patient
options.B: It means you never have to listen to breath sounds with a stethoscope
options.C: It guarantees the patient will be off the machine by morning
options.D: It ensures the machine supports breathing safely without injuring the lungs

explanation: Tracking pressures helps prevent lung damage (barotrauma) while making sure the patient gets enough oxygen. Safety first!

question: A patient wants to enter an SNF simply because they feel lonely at home and need help cooking meals. Why might this admission be delayed or denied coverage?

options.A: Social workers are not allowed to review home situations
options.B: The patient lacks a need for daily skilled nursing or therapy services
options.C: Medicare covers custodial care for anyone requesting it
options.D: The facility only accepts patients with infectious diseases

question: Why is it so important for the local community to actively take part in health programs?

options.C: It legally binds the local government to fund the health center indefinitely

explanation: Exactly! When community members help plan a project, they feel a sense of ownership and are much more likely to keep it running successfully.

question: Which of these is NOT a non-probability sampling method?

options.D: Purposive sampling

explanation: Correct! Simple random sampling belongs to the probability family because it relies on pure chance, not convenience or choice.

question: How soon can a woman's fertility return after an abortion or pregnancy loss?

options.A: As early as two weeks
options.B: Only after regular menses resume for a full year
options.C: Fertility does not return until age forty
options.D: After exactly six months

question: Which kitchen habit helps prevent accidental grease or boiling water spills?

options.A: Using metal spoons for all cooking tasks
options.B: Turning pot handles inward toward the stove back
options.C: Leaving burners on high heat while cleaning
options.D: Placing hot oil pans near the edge of the counter

explanation: Turning handles inward keeps pots out of reach of children and prevents adults from accidentally bumping into them. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h4)

question: Which tiny flap of tissue stops food from accidentally entering your windpipe (trachea) when you swallow?

options.A: The vocal cords
options.B: The lower esophageal sphincter
options.C: The epiglottis
options.D: The soft palate

question: A lab machine sends blood test results straight into a patient's electronic chart without losing data. What makes this smooth transfer possible?

options.A: Manual data re-entry
options.B: Physical paper filing
options.C: Higher computer screen resolution
options.D: Interoperability standards

question: What is the process of assigning numbers to qualitative categories called?

options.A: Data coding
options.B: Data graphing
options.C: Data cleaning
options.D: Data scaling

explanation: Coding is the translation of descriptive categories into numerical codes to make computer entry and statistical analysis straightforward. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which of these actions goes against professional nursing ethics in the workplace?

options.A: Providing emergency first aid to a worker who cut their hand
options.B: Disclosing an employee's private medical diagnosis to management without consent
options.C: Educating staff members on proper manual lifting techniques
options.D: Reporting a dangerous chemical spill to the company safety officer

explanation: Patient confidentiality is sacred. Sharing a worker's private medical details with bosses without permission is a serious breach of nursing ethics.

question: Which of the following is a known risk of poorly managed government price controls?

options.A: Supermarkets will automatically lower prices on all luxury items
options.B: Agricultural land will turn into high-yield forest reserves
options.C: Farmers may stop growing crops if prices do not cover production costs
options.D: Consumers will completely stop purchasing staple foods

explanation: If price caps are set too low, farmers lose money and reduce future production, causing scarcity. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h5)

question: Your patient looks drowsy, confused, and is working hard just to breathe using their neck muscles. What is your best next step?

options.A: Apply a standard nasal cannula with low flow
options.B: Prepare for immediate respiratory support
options.C: Encourage the patient to sleep it off
options.D: Wait for laboratory blood test results

explanation: When a patient is this exhausted and using accessory muscles, they are tiring out fast. Getting respiratory support ready right away can save their life!

question: A pregnant teenager at her antenatal visit says her family expects a local nurse to circumcise her newborn daughter. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Send the family to a traditional cutter who uses sterile tools
options.B: Offer to do it quietly at the clinic to avoid infections
options.C: Ignore it since cultural practices are none of a nurse's business
options.D: Educate the mother firmly on the severe health risks and legal penalties of FGM

explanation: Spot on! Nurses must actively educate patients against FGM, uphold professional ethics, and make it clear that medicalized cutting is both illegal and unethical.

question: What is the basic function of the internet?

options.A: Printing out patient care plans automatically
options.B: Generating electrical power for medical machines
options.C: Connecting computers globally to share information instantly
options.D: Storing physical files inside a hospital filing cabinet

explanation: The internet is a global network designed primarily to link computers together so data can travel freely between them. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h1)

question: Which patient might have a high Body Mass Index (BMI) classification that does NOT accurately reflect excess body fat?

options.A: An elderly patient experiencing severe muscle wasting
options.B: A malnourished child with chronic protein deficiency
options.C: A professional weightlifter with high muscle mass
options.D: A sedentary patient with advanced kidney disease

explanation: Muscle tissue is much denser than fat, meaning very muscular people can have a high BMI despite having low body fat. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h6)

question: What is the main job of UNOCHA during an international crisis?

options.A: Directly manufacturing and distributing pharmaceutical drugs
options.B: Coordinating humanitarian relief efforts among multiple organizations
options.C: Training local nurses in bedside clinical procedures
options.D: Providing armed military defense for disaster zones

explanation: Spot on! UNOCHA acts like the ultimate coordinator, making sure all the different groups rushing to help are working together smoothly.

question: What is the main difference between disease incidence and disease prevalence?

options.A: Incidence measures deaths, while prevalence measures recoveries.
options.B: Incidence counts only new cases, while prevalence counts all existing cases.
options.C: Prevalence is only used for acute infections, while incidence is for chronic illnesses.

explanation: Think of incidence as new arrivals over a period, while prevalence is a snapshot of everyone currently carrying the condition at a given time.

question: Which of these is NOT a main goal for a community nurse working to prevent disease?

options.A: Promoting local participation in mass immunization campaigns
options.B: Enforcing mandatory fines for community members who refuse treatment
options.C: Teaching residents how to identify and clear mosquito breeding sites
options.D: Educating families on safe food storage and personal hygiene habits

explanation: Nurses are educators, caregivers, and advocates. Handing out fines and police enforcement is up to legal authorities, not the nursing team!

question: A nurse wants to see if patient age relates to how often falls happen, without changing anything or giving any treatment. Which design fits best?

options.A: Correlational design
options.B: True experimental design
options.C: Clinical intervention trial
options.D: Qualitative ethnography

explanation: Great job if you picked correlational! This design simply looks at how two variables relate to each other in the real world, without the researcher interfering.

question: What is a major advantage of field research over laboratory research?

options.A: It gives the researcher total control over the weather
options.B: It requires no permission from ethics committees
options.C: It eliminates all possible errors in data entry
options.D: It reflects real-world conditions and natural behaviors

explanation: Brilliant! Field research happens out in natural settings, making the findings much easier to relate to everyday human life. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T4#GNS217_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which cranial nerve travels way past the neck to control organs in the chest and belly?

options.A: Optic nerve
options.B: Trigeminal nerve
options.C: Hypoglossal nerve
options.D: Vagus nerve

question: Why is accepting a patient's friend request on personal social media discouraged for nurses?

options.A: It automatically shares the nurse's bank account details with the patient
options.B: It slows down the hospital's internet connection speed
options.C: It blurs the boundary between a professional relationship and a personal one
options.D: It violates copyright laws regarding medical textbooks

explanation: Maintaining clear professional boundaries is essential for safe nursing practice and protects both the nurse and the patient. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h7)

question: What do we call wound drainage that is clear and watery?

options.A: Sanguineous
options.B: Fibrinous
options.C: Purulent
options.D: Serous

question: What is the main job of global health funding groups like Gavi or the Global Fund?

options.A: Collecting local taxes from rural market traders to build city hospitals
options.B: Enforcing strict criminal laws against medical malpractice in private clinics
options.C: Directly managing the daily nursing schedules of government health workers
options.D: Pooling resources from multiple sources to buy vaccines and medicines on a large scale

explanation: These global funds collect money from various countries to buy large quantities of essential medicines and vaccines for developing nations.

question: What is the golden rule of ethics when doing research with human beings?

options.A: Ensuring participants pay for taking part in the study
options.B: Keeping the true purpose of the study a secret forever
options.C: Publishing the real names of every patient in the local newspaper
options.D: Protecting participants from harm and respecting their autonomy

explanation: You nailed it! Patient safety, voluntary choice, and dignity always come first—before any research data.

question: What is the main advantage of teamwork between doctors, nurses, and dietitians in clinical nutrition?

options.A: Ensuring that the doctor makes all decisions without team input
options.B: Eliminating the need for nursing documentation on patient wards
options.C: Preventing gaps in care through shared expertise and communication
options.D: Reducing the number of working hours required for hospital staff

explanation: You got it! When healthcare professionals share their skills and communicate openly, patient care becomes much safer and more effective.

question: What is the main problem in a person with osteomalacia?

options.A: Excessive breakdown of cartilage by osteoclasts

options.C: Autoimmune destruction of the synovial lining

question: A patient knows her diet is unhealthy and plans to start eating vegetables next week, but hasn't bought any yet. Which stage is she in?

options.A: Precontemplation
options.B: Preparation
options.C: Maintenance
options.D: Action

question: Why does a woman usually reach a higher blood alcohol concentration than a man after drinking the exact same amount?

options.A: Men possess specialized liver filters that instantly destroy ethanol

options.C: Women generally have less body water and lower gastric enzyme activity
options.D: Men store all excess alcohol in fat tissue instead of the bloodstream

explanation: Because women typically have less total body water and lower levels of stomach enzymes to break down alcohol, more of it enters the bloodstream faster.

question: What does professional 'accountability' mean for a nurse on duty?

options.A: It shifts all blame for mistakes to the supervising senior nurse
options.B: It requires the hospital management to answer for patient complaints
options.C: It limits the nurse to performing only basic bedside tasks
options.D: It means taking personal responsibility for actions and care outcomes

explanation: Accountability is simply owning your work! When you make a clinical decision or care for a patient, you stand by the results of your actions.

question: Which metabolic process involves building complex body tissues from simpler substances?

options.A: Excretion

options.D: Digestion

question: A farmer arrives at the clinic with severe muscle twitching and too much saliva after working in the fields. What caused this?

options.A: A natural disaster caused by flooding

question: What is the main purpose of a tactical plan in a healthcare setting?

options.C: To punish staff who fail to meet quotas
options.D: To dictate minute-by-minute patient care tasks

question: Which physical sign strongly points to pelvic inflammation around the Pouch of Douglas?

question: Why is avoiding power struggles important when caring for a patient with a personality challenge?

options.A: Arguing escalates tension and rarely changes rigid behavioral patterns

options.C: Patients always win arguments because nurses are legally not allowed to speak
options.D: Winning a power struggle cures the patient's underlying psychiatric condition instantly

question: Which healthcare professional primarily helps a child with cerebral palsy learn how to perform daily living tasks like eating and dressing independently?

options.A: Respiratory therapist
options.B: Physical therapist
options.C: Speech pathologist
options.D: Occupational therapist

question: Besides sharing new rules, what must effective communication include during a healthcare transition?

options.A: An explanation of why the change improves patient outcomes

question: Which phase of disaster management involves strengthening hospital buildings so they can survive an earthquake?

question: What is a major cause of post-harvest food loss in farming communities?

question: A nurse implements strict handwashing and ensures a clean, well-ventilated ward to prevent infection outbreaks. Whose historical principles are being applied here?

options.A: Hippocrates
options.B: Florence Nightingale
options.C: Ransome-Kuti

question: Why should a nurse avoid abruptly stopping a patient's compulsive ritual?

question: What key detail does a drug label tell you about its strength?

question: In Nigeria, what color of bin liner is normally used for ordinary, non-hazardous general waste?

question: What is the key target recommended by the Abuja Declaration for national health budgets?

question: A patient is transferred from a rural clinic to a city teaching hospital. How does an interoperable EHR system help the nurse?

question: A client suddenly shows a change in pupil size and a dropping GCS score. What does this most likely indicate?

question: What happens in the brain during a seizure that puts cells at risk of injury?

question: Why should you avoid heavy medical jargon when teaching a family caregiver?

question: Which amino acid do renal tubule cells break down to produce ammonia and help buffer acid?

question: What is the best approach for a nurse who wants to explore a patient's spiritual needs?

question: Why does a strong primary health care system help major teaching hospitals?

question: How does it affect disaster response when agencies work in isolated 'silos'?

options.C: They protect their own budgets and authority instead of sharing resources

question: Why should soft pillows and stuffed animals be kept out of an infant's crib?

question: No matter how advanced hospital technology gets, what will always remain the nurse's primary challenge?

options.A: Balancing machine intelligence with compassionate human care
options.B: Finding enough electrical outlets to charge wearable patches

question: What is the main goal of nursing care when we want to help a patient improve their adaptation skills?

options.A: To ensure the patient relies permanently on hospital staff

options.C: To replace maladaptive habits with healthy coping skills

question: Which interface type allows a nurse to dictate clinical notes hands-free?

question: A rural village finally gets a new health center and local nurses. What economic factor made this possible?

question: How do nurses usually record how much of a meal a patient actually ate in the chart?

question: Which skin-dwelling cell releases histamine when an early inflammation or allergy starts?

question: A nurse is getting ready to clean a blood pressure cuff used on a patient with unbroken skin. What level of cleaning is enough?

question: What is the most common cause of primary hyperparathyroidism?

options.A: Severe dietary calcium deficiency

question: Why is poor nutrition (malnutrition) such a big problem during cancer treatment?

question: How do sudden altitude changes during an air medical evacuation affect a patient?

question: Why are unsafe injection practices such a big public health problem?

question: How does human relations theory change the daily role of a nurse manager?

question: Why do we include a reference list at the end of a report?

question: Where do isolation precautions mostly try to break the chain of infection?

question: What is the main reason healthcare workers should NOT recap needles after giving an injection?

question: Which part of the brain acts as the direct link between the nervous system and the endocrine system?

question: Which group of mental health conditions features overwhelming fear and ongoing distress?

question: When should respiratory hygiene measures start for a patient visiting the hospital?

question: Why does a patient with too much carbon dioxide in their body (hypercapnia) naturally start breathing much faster and deeper?
